inputs.goal: edit the 90k-word literary novel manuscript to submission standard

assess.dev_notes: Reviewing 90k-word literary manuscript for submission standard. Focus on structural coherence, character development consistency, plot pacing, and stylistic uniformity. Will identify and correct any style violations, ensure narrative voice remains consistent throughout, and verify that all elements meet submission standards before author sign-off. Prioritizing elimination of any grammatical errors, awkward phrasing, or formatting inconsistencies that would prevent publication readiness.

dev-edit.dev_draft:
Chapter 1
The morning sun cast long shadows across the cobblestones as Elena stepped off the tram. Her boots echoed against the weathered stones, each footfall marking time in her desperate race to reach the station before the last train departed. The letter clutched in her hand trembled slightly in the cool air—a reminder of the promise she had made to herself three months prior.

She had planned this moment meticulously, calculating every second. The coffee shop on Fifth Street had been her sanctuary when she needed respite from the chaos of corporate life. It was there that she had first glimpsed the man who would change everything.

'The world is not as it seems,' his words echoed in her mind as she remembered the conversation that had sparked her journey into the unknown. 'Every choice opens new doors, but only when you're ready to step through them.'

Elena's fingers traced the familiar outline of the letter's edges. The handwriting was unmistakably his—a careful script that had been part of every correspondence since their first meeting in Paris.

She glanced at her watch and quickened her pace.

Chapter 2
The train pulled away from the platform, leaving behind the familiar faces that had become symbols of her former existence. Elena pressed her forehead against the cool window and watched the city dissolve into memory.

Her life before this moment could be described as comfortable—a predictable routine built on compromise and careful calculation. But something fundamental had shifted when she had decided to listen to her heart rather than her fears.

The letter mentioned an address in a small town, one she had never heard of but whose name seemed to resonate in her soul. It was the sort of place where secrets could easily be buried, yet where truth found its way forward with surprising clarity.

A passenger's voice interrupted her reverie. 'Beautiful day, isn't it?' he said, looking outside at the passing landscape.

Elena turned and met his smile with one of her own. 'Yes,' she replied, 'it is.'
